examples.en: My friend teased me, so I fired back with a smile.
You shouldn't talk back to adults like that.
If my younger sibling says something, I always snap back.
He couldn't rebut the criticism calmly.

examples.ko: 상대 팀 감독의 말을 선수가 바로 되받아쳤어요.
examples.en: The player immediately answered back to the opposing coach's remark.

examples.ko: 면접관의 날카로운 질문을 논리적으로 되받아쳐서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that he countered the interviewer's sharp question so logically.

explain: '반박하다'는 격식 있는 말이고, '되받아치다'는 상대가 한 말에 바로 맞받아 말할 때 쓰는 구어체예요. 말대꾸처럼 버릇없게 들릴 때도 있어서 어른에게 쓰면 조심해야 해요.
explain_en: '반박하다' is formal, while '되받아치다' is a spoken word for answering back right away to what someone just said. It can sound like rude backtalk, so be careful when it is about an elder.

examples.ko: 그 노래를 들으니 옛 기억이 되살아났어요.
examples.en: Hearing that song brought my old memories back to life.

examples.ko: 죽은 줄 알았던 화분이 물을 줬더니 되살아났어요.
examples.en: The plant I thought was dead came back to life after I watered it.

examples.ko: 봄이 오면 얼어붙은 땅이 다시 되살아나요.
examples.en: When spring comes, the frozen ground comes back to life.

examples.ko: 되살아난 불씨 때문에 소방관들이 다시 출동했어요.
examples.en: The firefighters were called out again because of the rekindled embers.

examples.ko: 걱정 마세요. 시간이 지나면 식욕도 되살아날 거예요.
examples.en: Don't worry. Your appetite will come back in time too.

examples.ko: 영화를 보는 동안 어린 시절의 설렘이 되살아나는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: While watching the movie, it felt like the excitement of my childhood was coming back.

explain: 기억·감정·희망·불씨처럼 사라졌던 것이 다시 생길 때 어울려요. 예문처럼 '되살아나다' 형태로 자주 쓰고, 일부러 다시 살리는 건 '되살리다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It fits memories, feelings, hope or embers that had faded and then return. It is often used in the form '되살아나다' as in the examples, while bringing something back on purpose is '되살리다'.

examples.ko: 소는 풀을 먹고 나서 되새김질을 해요.
examples.en: Cows chew their cud after eating grass.
Camels are also animals that chew their cud.

examples.ko: 양들이 풀밭에 앉아 되새김질을 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The sheep are sitting on the grass chewing their cud.

examples.ko: 되새김질은 위가 여러 칸인 동물에게서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Cud-chewing can be seen in animals with a multi-chambered stomach.
I watched a cow chewing its cud for a long while.

examples.ko: 아이가 되새김질이 뭐냐고 물어서 소 이야기를 해 줬어요.
examples.en: My child asked what cud-chewing is, so I told a story about cows.

explain: 동물이 삼킨 먹이를 다시 입으로 올려 씹는 것을 말하고, 비유로 지난 일을 자꾸 다시 생각한다는 뜻으로도 써요. 과학에서는 '반추'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to animals bringing swallowed food back up to chew again, and figuratively to going over past events again and again. In science it is also called '반추'.

examples.en: The cow lies down and slowly chews its cud.

examples.ko: 염소가 풀을 삼킨 뒤 다시 되새김질하고 있어요.
examples.en: After swallowing the grass, the goat is chewing the cud again.

examples.ko: 어제 있었던 일을 계속 되새김질하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't keep ruminating on what happened yesterday.
If you keep ruminating on failure, you only feel heavier.
I walked home turning over what my teacher said.
Animals that chew their cud usually eat grass.

explain: 동물에게 쓰면 말 그대로 되새김질을 한다는 말이고, 사람에게 쓰면 지난 일이나 말을 계속 떠올린다는 느낌이 있어요. 비슷한 '곱씹다', '되씹다'와 바꿔 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: For animals it is literal chewing of the cud, while for people it gives the feeling of repeatedly recalling past events or words. It is often interchangeable with similar words like '곱씹다' and '되씹다'.

examples.ko: 그 말이 마음에 걸려서 계속 되씹게 돼요.
examples.en: That remark bothers me, so I keep dwelling on it.

examples.ko: 친구가 한 말을 집에 와서도 되씹었어요.
examples.en: I kept replaying what my friend said even after I got home.
There's no use brooding over past mistakes.
I lost sleep mulling over the boss's one remark.
Stop going over it like that and just forget it now.

examples.ko: 면접에서 한 대답을 되씹다가 밤을 새웠어요.
examples.en: I stayed up all night going over my answers from the interview.

explain: 음식을 다시 씹는다는 뜻도 있지만, 대화에서는 들은 말이나 지난 일을 마음속에서 자꾸 떠올린다는 뜻으로 더 많이 써요. 비슷한 '곱씹다'는 깊이 생각하는 느낌도 있지만, '되씹다'는 마음에 걸려서 반복해서 생각하는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It can mean chewing food again, but in conversation it is used more for replaying words you heard or past events in your mind. The similar '곱씹다' can feel like thinking deeply, while '되씹다' leans toward repeating something that bothers you.

examples.en: A heavy frost fell overnight and the cabbages froze.
The heavy autumn frost ruined the pepper crop.

examples.ko: 된서리가 내리기 전에 고구마를 캐야 해요.
examples.en: We have to dig up the sweet potatoes before the heavy frost comes.
I'm worried because the heavy frost came early this year.

examples.ko: 아침에 밭에 나가 보니 된서리로 하얗게 덮여 있었어요.
examples.en: When I went out to the field in the morning, it was covered white with heavy frost.

examples.ko: 갑자기 불어닥친 불황에 가게들이 된서리를 맞았어요.
examples.en: Shops were hit hard by the sudden downturn.

explain: 늦가을에 농작물이 상할 만큼 아주 세게 내리는 서리예요. 일상에서는 '된서리를 맞다'라는 비유로 더 자주 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 새로 낸 가게가 갑작스러운 불경기로 된서리를 맞았어요.
phrases.en: The newly opened shop was hit hard by the sudden recession.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 크게 타격을 받거나 큰 피해를 입을 때 써요. 주로 일, 사업, 계획에 나쁜 일이 닥쳤을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone or something suddenly takes a heavy blow or suffers great damage. It is mostly said when something bad hits work, business or plans.

explain_en: It is a very heavy frost in late autumn, strong enough to damage crops. In daily life you are more likely to hear it in the figurative expression '된서리를 맞다'.

examples.ko: 감기에 된통 걸려서 일주일 동안 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: I caught a terrible cold and lay in bed for a week.
I got a real scolding from my manager yesterday.
I started a business and got burned badly.
I slipped on the ice and landed hard on my backside.
I got caught badly by my mom while lying.
I fell on the street and got badly hurt.

explain: '몹시, 심하게'라는 느낌이지만 주로 감기에 걸리다, 혼나다, 당하다처럼 나쁜 일에 써요. '아주'는 어디에나 쓰지만 '된통'은 좋은 일에는 쓰지 않고, 편한 대화에서 많이 써요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of 'badly, severely' and is mostly used with bad things such as catching a cold, being scolded or getting burned. Unlike the all-purpose '아주', '된통' is not used for good things and is common in casual conversation.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 됨됨이가 바르다고 소문이 났어요.
examples.en: He has a reputation for being a person of good character.

examples.ko: 아이의 됨됨이는 부모를 보면 알 수 있다고 해요.
examples.en: They say you can tell a child's character by looking at the parents.

examples.ko: 한 번 만나 보니 됨됨이가 참 좋은 청년이었어요.
examples.en: After meeting him once, I found he was a young man of really good character.

examples.ko: 사람을 뽑을 때는 실력보다 됨됨이를 먼저 봐요.
examples.en: When hiring, I look at character before skill.
I carefully checked the quality of the item before buying it.

examples.ko: 말투만 들어도 됨됨이를 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tell someone's character just by how they speak.

explain: '성격'이 타고난 기질이라면 '됨됨이'는 사람의 품행과 인품이 어떤지를 보는 말이에요. '됨됨이가 바르다/좋다/못되다'처럼 평가하는 말과 함께 쓰고, 물건이 얼마나 잘 만들어졌는지를 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: While '성격' is about temperament, '됨됨이' is about how good a person's conduct and character are. It goes with evaluating words like '바르다', '좋다' and '못되다', and can also describe how well something is made.

examples.ko: 사고로 두개골에 금이 갔지만 다행히 회복했어요.
examples.en: His skull was fractured in the accident, but fortunately he recovered.
I saw a dinosaur skull fossil at the museum.
The skull protects the brain.
A helmet helps keep your skull from being injured.
The doctor examined the skull closely on the X-ray.

examples.ko: 해골 모형의 두개골이 진짜 같아서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The skull of the skeleton model looked so real that I was startled.

explain: 병원이나 과학 수업에서 쓰는 말이고, 쉬운 우리말로는 '머리뼈'라고 해요. '해골'은 죽은 사람의 머리뼈나 뼈 전체를 가리켜서 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: This is the word used in hospitals and science classes, and the plain Korean equivalent is '머리뼈'. '해골' refers to the bones of a dead person's head or the whole skeleton, so the feeling is different.

examples.en: I received a generous bonus, so I'm in a good mood.

examples.ko: 날씨가 추우니까 옷을 두둑이 껴입고 나가세요.
examples.en: It's cold, so bundle up thickly before you go out.

examples.ko: 할머니는 손님에게 음식을 두둑이 싸 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma packed plenty of food for the guest.
Business went well and I made a good amount of money.

examples.ko: 시험 전에 밥을 두둑이 먹고 갔어요.
examples.en: I ate a hearty meal before the exam and went.
Thank you for giving me such generous pocket money.

explain: 두껍고 넉넉하다는 느낌으로, 돈·음식·옷처럼 양이 충분할 때 써요. 형용사 '두둑하다'(지갑이 두둑하다)와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It conveys a thick, ample feeling and is used when there is plenty of something, like money, food or clothing. It is useful to learn it together with the adjective '두둑하다' (as in '지갑이 두둑하다').

examples.ko: 하늘에 흰 구름이 두둥실 떠 있어요.
examples.en: White clouds are floating gently in the sky.
The balloon floated up into the sky.
The full moon rose softly above the mountain.
A boat drifts lightly on the water.
The kids chased the soap bubbles floating away.

examples.ko: 튜브를 타고 바다에 두둥실 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: I lay floating on the sea in a tube.

explain: 구름, 달, 풍선, 배처럼 가볍게 떠 있는 모습을 말할 때 써요. '둥둥'보다 부드럽고 편안한 느낌이라 '떠 있다', '떠오르다'와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes things like clouds, the moon, balloons and boats floating lightly. It feels softer and more relaxed than '둥둥' and goes well with '떠 있다' and '떠오르다'.

examples.en: I ate shrimp and broke out in hives all over.

examples.ko: 약을 먹고 두드러기가 심해져서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My hives got worse after taking the medicine, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 두드러기가 나면 가려워서 자꾸 긁게 돼요.
examples.en: When you get hives, it itches and you keep scratching.
I'm worried because hives have come up on my child's arm.
Hives sometimes go away after a few days.

examples.ko: 꽃가루 때문에 두드러기가 생기는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people get hives from pollen.

explain: 음식이나 약, 꽃가루 같은 알레르기 때문에 피부가 붉게 부풀고 가려운 증상이에요. '두드러기가 나다/생기다/올라오다'처럼 쓰고, 소리가 비슷한 '두드러지다'(눈에 띄다)와 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It is a red, swollen, itchy skin reaction, often caused by allergies to food, medicine or pollen. It is used as '두드러기가 나다/생기다/올라오다', and don't confuse it with the similar-sounding '두드러지다' (to stand out).

examples.ko: 옆방에서 사람들이 두런두런 이야기하는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear people talking in low voices in the next room.

examples.ko: 부엌에서 엄마와 이모가 두런두런 얘기를 나눠요.
examples.en: Mom and my aunt are chatting quietly in the kitchen.
Since dawn there was a low murmur of voices in the yard.
We talked softly about old times all night.
The murmur of voices woke me up.

examples.ko: 할머니들이 마루에 앉아 두런두런 이야기를 나누고 계세요.
examples.en: The grandmothers are sitting on the porch chatting in low voices.

explain: 여럿이 낮은 목소리로 조용히 이야기하는 소리나 모습이에요. '소곤소곤'은 비밀 이야기처럼 아주 작게 말하는 느낌이고, '두런두런'은 정답고 편안하게 이야기하는 분위기예요.
explain_en: It describes several people talking quietly in low voices. '소곤소곤' feels like whispering a secret, while '두런두런' has a warm, relaxed atmosphere.

examples.en: I drew water up from the well with a bucket.
The bucket was so heavy that I pulled it up with all my strength.

examples.ko: 할아버지 댁 마당에는 오래된 우물과 두레박이 있어요.
examples.en: In Grandpa's yard there is an old well and a well bucket.
When I dropped the bucket, there was a splash.

examples.ko: 민속촌에서 두레박으로 물 긷는 체험을 했어요.
examples.en: I tried drawing water with a well bucket at the folk village.

examples.ko: 두레박 줄이 짧아서 물이 닿지 않았어요.
examples.en: The bucket rope was short, so it didn't reach the water.

explain: 우물물을 줄로 내려 퍼 올리는 그릇이에요. 지금은 옛이야기, 동화, 민속촌에서 주로 만나요. 물을 '긷다'는 'ㄷ' 불규칙이라 '길어요'로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It is a bucket lowered on a rope to scoop water from a well. Today you mostly meet it in old tales, fairy tales and folk villages. The verb for drawing water, '긷다', is a ㄷ-irregular verb and becomes '길어요'.

examples.ko: 설날에 할아버지는 한복 위에 두루마기를 입으셨어요.
examples.en: On New Year's Day, Grandpa wore a durumagi over his hanbok.
In winter a durumagi is warm, so people wear it like a coat.
I wore a durumagi to the wedding.
The durumagi sleeves were long, so I rolled them up.

examples.ko: 아버지가 새 두루마기를 맞추러 한복집에 가셨어요.
examples.en: My father went to the hanbok shop to have a new durumagi made.
I saw a Joseon-era durumagi at the museum.

explain: 한복 위에 입는 겉옷으로, 외투처럼 입는 옷이에요. 화장실에서 쓰는 '두루마리 휴지'의 '두루마리'(둘둘 만 것)와 소리가 비슷하니 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It is an outer garment worn over hanbok, like an overcoat. Don't confuse it with '두루마리' (something rolled up), as in '두루마리 휴지' (toilet paper roll), which sounds similar.

en: looking around; glancing this way and that

examples.ko: 아이가 낯선 곳에서 두리번두리번 주위를 살폈어요.
examples.en: The child looked around this way and that in the unfamiliar place.
I looked all around, but I couldn't see my wallet.

examples.ko: 신입생이 교실 앞에서 두리번두리번 누군가를 찾았어요.
examples.en: The new student looked around in front of the classroom for someone.

examples.ko: 강아지가 두리번두리번 둘러보더니 제 옆에 앉았어요.
examples.en: The puppy glanced around and then sat next to me.

examples.ko: 관광객이 지도를 들고 두리번두리번 거리를 둘러봐요.
examples.en: A tourist holding a map looks around the street in all directions.
While looking around here and there, my eyes met my friend's.

explain: 고개를 이리저리 돌리며 주변을 살피는 모습이에요. 대화에서는 '두리번거리다'라고 동사로 많이 말하니 함께 알아 두세요. 길을 찾거나 누군가를 찾을 때, 낯선 곳에서 어색할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes turning your head this way and that to look around. In conversation the verb '두리번거리다' is commonly used, so learn it together. It suits situations like looking for a way or a person, or feeling awkward in an unfamiliar place.

examples.en: When I asked, my friend helped without a word of objection.
The owner gave me a refund without any fuss.

examples.ko: 엄마가 말하자 동생은 두말없이 방을 치웠어요.
examples.en: When Mom spoke, my younger sibling cleaned the room without complaint.
At that price, I'll buy it without a second thought.
I did what my senior told me without complaint.
Thank you for following me without any objection.

explain: 불평이나 반대 없이 바로 따르거나 받아들일 때 써요. 비슷한 '군말 없이'는 불평만 하지 않는 느낌이고, '두말없이'는 망설임 없이 바로 한다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone goes along with something immediately, without complaint or objection. The similar '군말 없이' stresses not grumbling, while '두말없이' leans more toward acting right away without hesitation.

examples.en: My grandmother was born and raised in a remote mountain village.

examples.ko: 두메산골이라 버스가 하루에 두 번밖에 안 와요.
examples.en: It's a remote mountain village, so the bus only comes twice a day.
Even remote mountain villages have the internet now.

examples.ko: 도시를 떠나 두메산골로 이사 갈까 해요.
examples.en: I'm thinking of leaving the city and moving to a remote mountain village.

examples.ko: 그 학교는 두메산골에 있는 작은 분교예요.
examples.en: That school is a small branch school in a remote mountain village.

examples.ko: 두메산골 마을에서 별이 정말 많이 보였어요.
examples.en: I could see so many stars in the remote mountain village.

explain: '시골'보다 더 깊고 외진 산속 마을을 말해요. 교통이 불편하고 사람이 적다는 느낌이 있어서, 옛날이야기나 어렸을 때 살던 곳을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to a village deeper in the mountains and more isolated than a '시골' (countryside). It suggests poor transport and few people, and often comes up in old stories or when talking about where someone lived as a child.

examples.en: As the seclusion dragged on, fans grew worried.

examples.ko: 작가는 두문불출 끝에 새 소설을 완성했어요.
examples.en: After a long seclusion, the author finished a new novel.

examples.ko: 두문불출 중인 친구에게 안부 메시지를 보냈어요.
examples.en: I sent a check-in message to my friend who is staying shut in.
He stayed shut in all vacation, so Mom is worried.
As his reclusion went on, rumors spread.

examples.ko: 두문불출 생활을 끝내고 오랜만에 밖으로 나왔어요.
examples.en: I ended my life of staying shut in and went outside for the first time in a long while.

explain: 집에 틀어박혀 밖에 나가지 않는 것을 뜻하는 네 글자 표현이에요. 뉴스나 글에서 유명인이나 작가가 모습을 보이지 않을 때 자주 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '집에 틀어박혀 있다'고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: This four-character expression means shutting yourself in and not going out. It often appears in news and writing when a celebrity or author is out of sight, while in everyday talk people say '집에 틀어박혀 있다'.

examples.ko: 그는 시험 기간 내내 집에서 두문불출했어요.
examples.en: He stayed shut in at home throughout the exam period.

examples.ko: 작가는 몇 달 동안 두문불출하며 소설을 썼어요.
examples.en: The author shut himself away for months and wrote a novel.
My friend has been staying shut in lately, and I'm worried.
The senior who had been shut in came to the gathering for the first time in a while.

examples.ko: 방학 때는 두문불출하지 말고 운동도 하세요.
examples.en: During vacation, don't stay holed up, and get some exercise too.

examples.ko: 그녀는 이사 온 뒤로 두문불출하고 있어요.
examples.en: She has been staying shut in since she moved here.

explain: 밖에 나가지 않고 집에만 있는 상태를 말하는 격식 있는 표현이에요. 편한 대화에서는 '집에 틀어박혀 있다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is a somewhat formal expression for staying home and not going out at all. In casual conversation '집에 틀어박혀 있다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: I was so nervous that my presentation went on without any order.
I'm sorry for speaking randomly, just as things came to mind.

examples.ko: 두서없이 쓴 글이라 읽기 힘들 수 있어요.
examples.en: It was written without structure, so it may be hard to read.
My excited friend poured out the story all jumbled.
I took notes with no order, so it was hard to organize them later.
I spoke in a disorganized way, but did you follow it?

explain: 말이나 글의 순서와 앞뒤가 맞지 않고 뒤죽박죽일 때 써요. '두서없이 말씀드려 죄송합니다'처럼 자신의 말을 낮추며 사과할 때도 자주 쓰고, '두서없는 말'처럼 형용사 형태로도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when speech or writing has no clear order or logic and feels jumbled. It is often used to apologize for your own rambling, as in '두서없이 말씀드려 죄송합니다', and also appears in the adjective form, as in '두서없는 말'.
